blocks.text: Gunpowder is a coarse blend of 75 per cent potassium nitrate, 15 per cent wood charcoal and 10 per cent sulfur. The charcoal carbon is the main fuel, the nitrate is the oxidiser, and sulfur is the additional fuel that makes the powder burn faster. On burning: 10KNO3(s) + 3S(s) + 8C(s) gives 2K2CO3(s) + 3K2SO4(s) + 6CO2(g) + 5N2(g).

blocks.prompt: Give the composition of gunpowder and the reaction of its combustion (exercise Q.2l), and explain why it explodes in a confined space.
blocks.explanation: 75 per cent KNO3, 15 per cent charcoal, 10 per cent sulfur; 10KNO3 + 3S + 8C gives 2K2CO3 + 3K2SO4 + 6CO2 + 5N2. The nitrate supplies its own oxygen, so the burning needs no air and is very fast, and the eleven moles of hot gas produced from solids expand violently when confined.

items: Gunpowder: 75% KNO3 (oxidiser), 15% charcoal (fuel), 10% S (extra fuel); 10KNO3 + 3S + 8C gives 2K2CO3 + 3K2SO4 + 6CO2 + 5N2.
